riskAssessment.reason: The renderer formats explicit upstream facts into an atomic Markdown message. The primary risks are accidental recomputation, Markdown/card truncation, and leakage into Publisher/provider concerns.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: Numeric limits are caller-supplied through TelegramRenderLimits because the request does not provide product-specific line or character values. The renderer rejects over-limit atomic output rather than truncating it.

acceptance: src/features/weekly_radar/interface/telegram_renderer.rs exposes a provider-agnostic Telegram Markdown summary boundary that consumes only explicit period, section item, company-card, System Health, and No Change facts and returns one immutable rendered message.

The rendered summary includes explicit Important Structural Change, Stage Transition, Top5, Threshold Distance, Rising, Dropped, System Health, and explicit No Change sections in deterministic priority order without computing or changing any supplied Stage, Ranking, Distance, or health value.

TelegramRenderLimits enforces caller-supplied character, line, section-item, and company-card limits before output; over-limit output returns a typed error and does not truncate Markdown, split a Markdown fragment, or truncate a company card.
Input validation rejects blank identities, companies, Markdown fragments, and contradictory explicit No Change plus change sections; repeated identities are rejected without mutating the input model.

Module-local, same-stem companion, and public integration tests cover every requested section, deterministic order, exact Markdown/card retention, No Change, limit failures, input validation, and provider isolation; no architecture test or global coverage policy is modified.

The WI spec, implementation plan, reference-impact evidence, active Summary, strict AI Cockpit Finish evidence, archive bundle, and local commit record the delivered boundary, verification, authorization, remaining non-goals, and local-only next action.

guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: The Weekly Radar has explicit upstream change and health facts, but it has no short, provider-agnostic Markdown view boundary for Telegram. Without an atomic renderer, a later publisher could silently truncate Markdown or company cards, or re-derive Stage, Ranking, Distance, or No Change while compressing the report.
constraints: Consume only explicit inputs; formatting may label and order supplied facts but must not calculate Stage, Ranking, Threshold Distance, Important Structural Change, Stage Transition, Top5, Rising, Dropped, System Health, or No Change.
Preserve full caller-supplied Markdown fragments and company cards. Enforce caller-supplied length and item limits by returning typed errors before producing output; do not truncate or split content.

Keep the renderer provider-agnostic and local to the Weekly Radar interface boundary. Do not implement delivery adapters, network clients, sensitive runtime configuration, retry, scheduling, persistence, or message splitting.

Complete Contract, spec/plan, TDD, focused/module-local/integration verification, strict AI Cockpit Finish, archive, and local commit. Do not push, open a PR, merge, close, or delete the remote branch.
intent.rationale: An explicit-input renderer boundary makes Telegram formatting deterministic and auditable while keeping message delivery and all domain calculations outside this WI. Atomic validation is the smallest safe way to honor message limits without damaging Markdown or company-card context.
